title: Run for counting a unary variable index
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B,n$ natural numbers, $s,b$ Booleans, $rest$ a finite bit string, and $st$ a machine state. Suppose the suffix of $x$ beginning at position $st.P$ is $n$ true bits followed by a false bit, then $b$, then $rest$; every register of $st$ is at most $B$; $|x|\le B$; and $st.V\le st.P$. Then the machine has a guarded run from label $\text{lc}(s)$ and state $st$ to label $\text{lv}(s,b)$ and the state obtained by setting $P=st.P+n+2$ and $V=st.V+n$, leaving the other registers unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: The suffix of $x$ at position $st.P$ is $n$ true bits, then false, then $b$, then $rest$
Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural-number register bound, $s,b\in\{0,1\}$,
and $r$ a finite bit string. Suppose that, from input position $P$ in a machine state
$t$, the remaining input consists of $n$ true bits, then a false bit, then $b$, followed
by $r$; every register of $t$ is at most $B$, $|x|\le B$, and the variable counter $V$
is at most $P$. The machine reaches the literal-evaluation phase with the same values of
$s$ and $b$, input position $P+n+2$, and variable counter $V+n$.
